recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-8551 because the current source carries the inclusive default and the later comparator support is a compatible refinement rather than a reversal.
issue_request: FHIR-8551 was Published with resolution Not Persuasive with Modification. It initially proposed an or-equal-to extension after SimpleQuantity removed Quantity.comparator from Observation.referenceRange.low/high, but the final disposition was to clarify that the low/high endpoint values are inclusive, e.g. >=5 - <=9, and not create the extension.
initial_application: August 2015 commits first pre-applied an inclusive-flag extension approach, then commit 593b20acf2bf6448693ef783462167a40d8780b3 applied the final disposition by changing Observation.referenceRange.low/high text to state inclusive endpoints. Later source refactoring moved the authoritative definition into source/observation/structuredefinition-Observation.xml.
additional_context: FHIR-5165 is the supporting Quantity/SimpleQuantity comparator split. FHIR-51566 later changed Observation.referenceRange.low/high to Quantity for R6 and allowed explicit inclusive/exclusive comparators, but preserved the FHIR-8551 inclusive default when comparators are absent. Zulip and OO minutes identify FHIR-8551 as related background for that later work.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current build-scoped Observation StructureDefinition already says absent low.comparator/high.comparator values are inclusive, allows explicit >= and <=, and uses > or < only for intended exclusive bounds.

related_jiras.note: Quantity/SimpleQuantity comparator handling caused Observation.referenceRange.low/high to need explicit inclusive wording.
R6 later allowed explicit Observation.referenceRange.low/high comparators while preserving FHIR-8551 inclusive defaults when comparators are absent.
